title: An etale sheaf with an atlas by algebraic spaces is an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathit{Sets}$ be a functor which is a sheaf for jointly surjective etale covering families: every family of sections agreeing on all pairwise fibre products glues uniquely. Etale morphisms are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose that an $S$-scheme $U$ and a natural transformation $q:h_U\to F$ are given, where $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$. Assume that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $a\in F(T)$, the functor $h_T\times_{a,F,q}h_U$ is represented by an algebraic space $P_a$ over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and its projection $P_a\to T$ is surjective and etale. These properties mean that for every representable etale scheme chart $V\to P_a$ the composite $V\to T$ is etale, and that some surjective etale scheme chart has composite surjective onto $T$. Then $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$ in the fppf-sheaf convention of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 0BH4 (lemma-spaces-etale-locally-representable), scheme-atlas specialization. The input is only an etale sheaf; the conclusion is an algebraic space in the fppf-sheaf convention.

proof.text: Write $q_H(u)$ for the section obtained by applying $q$ to an $S$-morphism $u:H\to U$. Apply the atlas hypothesis with $T=U$ and $a=q_U(\mathrm{id}_U)$. It gives an algebraic space $R$ whose functor of points is $R(H)=\{(u,v)\in h_U(H)^2:q_H(u)=q_H(v)\}$. Let $s,t:R\to h_U$ be its two projections. One projection is chartwise etale by hypothesis; interchange $(u,v)$ to obtain the other. The map $j=(s,t):R\to h_{U\times_SU}$ is a monomorphism, because a pair determines an element of $R(H)$ uniquely. Its image on each $H$ is an equivalence relation: equality of the two $q_H$-images is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. The diagonal pair $(u,u)$ gives a section of either projection.

source.place: Tag 0BH4, first three proof sentences: form the relation R=U times_F U; scheme-atlas specialization.

proof.text: We check that $j$ is locally of finite type without assuming any finiteness or separation of $U/S$. For every representable etale scheme chart $V\to R$, the composite $V\to U$ through $s$ is etale by the hypothesis on $P_a$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], every point of $V$ has an affine open neighbourhood mapping into an affine open of $U$ whose coordinate ring is finitely presented, hence finitely generated, over that of the affine open of $U$. Postcomposing $j$ with the first projection $p_1:U\times_SU\to U$ gives $s$. Let $W^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}B^{\prime}$ be an arbitrary affine open of $U\times_SU$ and $v\in V$ a point mapping into $W^{\prime}$. Choose an affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U$ containing the image of $v$ in $U$, a principal open $W=D(b)=\operatorname{Spec}B^{\prime}_b\subseteq W^{\prime}\cap p_1^{-1}(U_0)$ containing the image of $v$, and an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}C\ni v$ of $V$ mapping into $W$ with $C$ finitely generated over $A$: start with a finite-type affine chart of $V\to U$ around $v$ over $U_0$, and shrink it to a principal affine open inside the inverse image of $W$; adjoining one inverse keeps finite generation over $A$. The ring maps factor as $A\to B^{\prime}_b\to C$, so the same finite set of $A$-algebra generators generates $C$ over $B^{\prime}_b$; adding $1/b$ to it generates $C$ over $B^{\prime}$. Thus the inverse image of every affine open $W^{\prime}$ is covered by spectra of finitely generated $B^{\prime}$-algebras, and $V\to U\times_SU$ is locally of finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], as required. This is the affine argument underlying Tag 0462.

source.place: Tag 0BH4 via Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), reduction (1) to (2); affine specialization of Tag 0462.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-monomorphism-separated-lqf] to $j:R\to U\times_SU$, using the monomorphism from step 1 and the chartwise finite-type verification from step 2. It makes $j$ separated and chartwise locally quasi-finite. The target $U\times_SU$ is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Therefore [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] gives a scheme representing $R$, over $U\times_SU$. Replace $R$ by that representing scheme; the identifications of its sections and projections from step 1 are preserved.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), reduction (1) to (2), invoking Tags 0463 and 03XX.

proof.text: Now the identity chart of the scheme $R$ shows that $s,t:R\to U$ are etale; their diagonal sections show that they are surjective. Thus $j$ is an etale equivalence relation in schemes. Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] and call its fppf quotient $Q$, with quotient map $\pi:h_U\to Q$. It gives all three facts needed below: $Q$ is an algebraic space, every section of $Q$ has etale-local lifts to $U$, and $h_R\simeq h_U\times_Qh_U$. In particular, for two maps $u,v:H\to U$, $\pi_H(u)=\pi_H(v)$ if and only if $(u,v)\in R(H)$, which by step 1 is equivalent to $q_H(u)=q_H(v)$.

source.place: Tag 0BH4, quotient construction; scheme relation presentation is Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation).

proof.text: The fppf sheaf $Q$ is also an etale sheaf: every jointly surjective family of etale scheme morphisms is a covering in [def-pc-fppf-site], because [def-weil-etale-morphism] says its maps are flat and locally of finite presentation. For $x\in Q(H)$ choose an etale covering $H_i\to H$ and lifts $u_i:H_i\to U$ supplied by [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. On each overlap $H_i\times_HH_j$, their images under $\pi$ agree, so the kernel-pair identity in that node gives a section of $R$ with these two endpoints. Hence $q(u_i)=q(u_j)$ on the overlap. The assumed etale sheaf axiom for $F$ glues them uniquely to a section $\phi_H(x)\in F(H)$.

source.place: Tag 0BH4, final comparison of etale quotients; its omitted small check, existence of the comparison.

proof.text: This construction is independent of its choices. Given two covering families and lifts of $x$, use the covering by their pairwise fibre products over $H$. On each member the two lifts have the same $\pi$-image, hence form an $R$-pair by [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]; their $q$-images agree. Uniqueness in the sheaf axiom of $F$ makes the two glued sections equal. Pulling a lifting cover back along $H^{\prime}\to H$ produces lifts of the restricted section; uniqueness again gives $\phi_{H^{\prime}}(x|_{H^{\prime}})=\phi_H(x)|_{H^{\prime}}$. Thus $\phi:Q\to F$ is natural and $\phi\pi=q$. The use of common refinements is on the small etale site of the scheme $H$, whose fibre products and covering structure are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site].

source.place: Tag 0BH4, final comparison: the omitted small check, independence and naturality.

proof.text: For injectivity, let $x,y\in Q(H)$ have $\phi_H(x)=\phi_H(y)$. Choose etale-local lifts to $U$ of both sections and a common refinement as in step 6. On this covering they are represented by $u,v$ with $q(u)=q(v)$. Step 1 says $(u,v)\in R$, and the kernel-pair identity of [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] gives $\pi(u)=\pi(v)$. Thus $x$ and $y$ agree on the covering, and separatedness of the etale sheaf $Q$ from step 5 gives $x=y$.

source.place: Tag 0BH4, final comparison: injectivity from equality of the two kernel pairs.

proof.text: For surjectivity, fix $a\in F(H)$. By the atlas hypothesis choose a representable surjective etale scheme chart $V\to P_a$ whose composite $V\to H$ is surjective and etale. The universal pair in $P_a=h_H\times_Fh_U$ gives a map $u:V\to U$ with $q(u)=a|_V$. The section $x_V=\pi(u)\in Q(V)$ satisfies $\phi_V(x_V)=a|_V$. Its two pullbacks to $V\times_HV$ have the same $\phi$-image, hence are equal by step 7 applied to that scheme. The etale sheaf axiom for $Q$ glues $x_V$ to $x\in Q(H)$. Naturality and separatedness of $F$ give $\phi_H(x)=a$. Thus every $\phi_H$ is a bijection, including on empty schemes, and their inverses are natural by the naturality already proved.

source.place: Tag 0BH4, final comparison: local surjectivity followed by explicit descent of the lifted section.

proof.text: The natural isomorphism $\phi:Q\simeq F$ proves the required conclusion in the fppf convention. Explicitly, an fppf matching family in $F$ transports by $\phi^{-1}$ to one in $Q$, glues there uniquely, and transports back. For two scheme sections of $F$, their fibre product is identified by $\phi^{-1}$ with the corresponding fibre product over $Q$, hence is a scheme because the diagonal of $Q$ is representable. Finally, since $\phi\pi=q$, every scheme base change of $q$ is the corresponding base change of the representable surjective etale atlas $\pi$ of $Q$. These are exactly the sheaf, diagonal and atlas clauses of [def-trf-algebraic-space].
